title: Why Do Some People See a Halo Around the Sun?

scenes.text: A bright 22‑degree halo circles the Sun on clear winter days!
Hexagonal ice crystals in high clouds refract sunlight at a 22‑degree angle.
scenes.label: ICE CRYSTAL REFRACTION
scenes.query2: how ice crystals create solar halo

scenes.text: The specific crystal orientation creates a bright inner circle and a fainter outer one.
scenes.label: ORIENTED CRYSTALS
scenes.query: crystal orientation sun halo inner outer ring

scenes.text: Meteorologists use halo sightings to predict upcoming weather fronts.
scenes.label: WEATHER PREDICTION TOOL
scenes.query2: halo as indicator of approaching storm
